note: Golden cases for the report prompt. Read by tests/test_report_prompt.py -- this file is load-bearing, not documentation. Each case names a scenario built from committed fixtures and the structural properties the descent payload must have before the prompt is rendered. Expected model output is asserted by shape and citation integrity only, never by prose. One case is composed rather than captured; see its `fixture_provenance` for why that is unavoidable rather than convenient.

observations.evidence_key: a key present in the input

cases.name: localised_cause
cases.source: the `broken` label -- PE2 isolated, both uplinks shut
cases.why: The chain is the product. A report naming the finding without the four rungs above it is an assertion; the chain is an argument an engineer can check link by link.

cases.name: cause_not_localised
cases.source: composed -- the `broken` label's bgp section over the `healthy` label's lower layers. Both halves are real captured output; only the combination is synthetic, and no consistently-behaving fabric can produce it.
cases.why: The finding most likely to be reported badly. The model will want to name the topmost broken rung as the cause; the descent has already established that it is not one. The prompt must carry the healthy lower rungs so the model can see there is nothing underneath rather than infer something.

fixture_provenance.why_not_captured: No consistently-behaving fabric can produce 'BGP session Idle while every layer beneath it is healthy'. If the transport, route, IGP and interface are all fine, the session comes up. That is simultaneously what makes cause_not_localised a finding worth having and what makes it impossible to capture from a real device.
fixture_provenance.what_is_real: Both halves are real captured output. The bgp section is the `broken` label's genuine Idle session; the transport/route/igp/interface sections are the `healthy` label's genuine healthy layers.
fixture_provenance.what_is_synthetic: Only the combination. No output was written, edited or invented -- two real captures are served to different rungs of one descent.
fixture_provenance.note: Every other golden case in this file is captured whole from one label. This is the single exception, and the reason is above rather than in a commit message, because a future reader comparing it against the others needs to know why.
fixture_provenance.round_3_attempt: Round 3 of the injection sequence (2026-08-16) was designed to replace this composed case with a captured one: a BGP neighbour administratively shut on PE2 with a healthy underlay. It produced `transport_blocked`, not `cause_not_localised` (OBS-092). The reason is sharper than this block's original 'no consistently-behaving fabric can produce it': rung 2 reads `connection_state` from `show bgp neighbor` while rung 1 reads state from `show bgp summary` -- TWO COMMANDS REPORTING THE SAME FSM. `cause_not_localised` needs rung 1 broken and rung 2 healthy, which requires the summary and the neighbour detail to disagree: an inconsistent device, not a fault. This case is composed BECAUSE IT HAS TO BE, not because capturing it was inconvenient -- and it stays composed until B-432 makes rung 2 independent or removes the finding.
fixture_provenance.b432_resolution: RESOLVED at B-432. Rung 2 now reads the SOCKET (`Socket ... armed for read`) rather than `connection_state`, which is the same finite state machine rung 1 reads from `show bgp summary`. The two are different subsystems, so `cause_not_localised` -- rung 1 broken with a live TCP transport beneath it -- is now REACHABLE: an AS mismatch, a capability mismatch, or an MD5 failure after TCP establishes all produce exactly that shape. This case stays composed only because no such fault has been captured yet, which is an ordinary gap in the corpus rather than a structural impossibility. It is now a candidate for a future injection round.

cases.name: refusal_path
cases.source: the `t0` label -- predates template capture, so the transport rung genuinely cannot be read
cases.why: The single most valuable thing the Constraints slot buys. A model that fills an unread rung with a plausible cause produces something indistinguishable from a finding -- the same silent-degradation shape as OBS-006, OBS-043 and OBS-044, arriving in the report layer.

refusal_note: GRACE's C slot requires a named refusal path. The marker differs per prompt because the refusals differ in kind: a report that cannot determine a cause returns `undetermined`, while a correlation with nothing to correlate returns `found: false`. Enforced by tests/test_prompts.py, which reads this field rather than assuming one vocabulary fits both.
